High level write sequence:
1. Poll Command register until doorbell bit is clear, indicating mailbox is not busy.
2. Write data into payload region. This may be large or small payload
3. Write data to the command register: Opcode, Subopcode, doorbell bit.
4. Poll Command register until doorbell bit is clear.
5. Read Status register
 a. If Comp bit is set, read the mailbox status.
 b. If Fail bit is set, return an error.
6. Return command status and mailbox status

High level read sequence:
1. Poll Command register until doorbell bit is clear, indicating mailbox is not busy.
2. (If command has any associated data in the read request) Write command data into small payload region.
3. Write data to the command register: Opcode, Subopcode, doorbell bit.
4. Poll Command register until doorbell bit is clear.
5. Read Status register
 a. If Comp bit is set, read the mailbox status.
 b. If Fail bit is set, return an error.
6. Read data from payload region
7. Return command status and mailbox status

-PTTI Guide.txt w/Robert Dzienisz

Assumptions:
- Test Service Wrapper is always 8 bytes long.
- After Test service Wrapper there is a command code specifying what command it is, e.g. 00 (Connect), 21 (Configure Device Under Test).
- In Test MCTP Frame Example we are sending [1, 129, 0, 4] frame to device with DUT Connection ID = 20 (14000000 hex - little endian).
- Time measuring for MCTP commands is not yet possible due to external factors, but it will be enabled soon (You might find the frame structure diffrent from what is in 0.4.0 spec - page 39)

Hardcoded values:
Test Client ID is 44434241 as for now, later we will implement a mechanism to genere it so it's diffrent every time you connect. 
Connect command- 74736474 is a Security Parameter, it can be longer (4 bytes preceding the parameter specify length in bytes- 04000000).
Test Service Capabilities are yet to be implemented so 14000000 in Configure Device Under Test RESPONSE is hardcoded as for now.


1. Connect
REQUEST:  00 FF 2031 00000000  00 04000000 74736574
	<Test Service Wrapper>
RESPONSE: 00 FF 2131 44434241 00 01 44434241

2. Configure Device Under Test
REQUEST:  00 FF 2031 44434241 21 10000000 00
RESPONSE: 00 FF 2131 44434241 00 14000000

3. Register to protocol
REQUEST:  00 FF 2031 44434241 22 00 14000000 00
RESPONSE: 00 FF 2131 44434241 00 14000000    

4.1  Test MCTP Frame
REQUEST:  00 00 2031 44434241 00 14000000 <MCTP MESSAGE in binary>
RESPONSE: 00 00 2131 44434241 <RESPONSE>

4.2 Test MCTP Frame EXAMPLE
REQUEST:  00 00 2031 44434241 14000000 01 81 00 04
RESPONSE: 00 00 2131 44434241 01 01 00 04 00 45 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 

5. Disconnect
REQUEST:  00 FF 2031 44434241 01
RESPONSE: 00 FF 2131 44434241 00

BOOT_IMAGE=(hd0,gpt2)/vmlinuz-4.18.0-193.el8.x86_64 root=/dev/mapper/cl-root ro crashkernel=1G resume=/dev/mapper/cl-swap rd.lvm.lv=cl/root rd.lvm.lv=cl/swap console=tty0 earlyprintk=ttyS0,115200 disable_mtrr_cleanup

2Eh + 000157h - Net Function = 2Eh-2Fh LUN = 00b
-	E8h        Restart MCTP Discovery
o	Request
?	Byte 1:3 = Intel Manufacturer ID - 000157h, LS byte first.
o	Response:
?	Byte 1 - Completion Code
?	=00h - Success (Remaining standard Completion Codes are shown in Section 2.15).
?	=D5h - MCTP discovery cannot be executed since system is not in S0 state
?	=FFh - Unspecified Error
o	Description:
?	This command restarts discovery of MCTP endpoints by Intel SPS FW as MCTP bus owner. All previously discovered endpoints will be removed from bus owner routing table. Intel SPS FW MCTP driver will execute full MCTP endpoint discovery process, starting with sending Prepare for Endpoint Discovery command, which will cause endpoints to reset internal Discovery Flag.
-	E9h        ACL Update Start
o	               Request
?	Byte 1:3 - Intel Manufacturer ID 000157h, LS byte first.
?	Byte 4:5 - Requesters PCIe 
?	Bus: Device: Function (BDF).
?	Byte4 contains Bus number, 
?	Byte5 contains Device: Function part of BDF.
o	Response
?	Response
?	Byte 1 - Completion Code
?	=00h - Success (Remaining standard Completion Codes are shown in Section 2.15).
?	=FFh - Unspecified Error
?	Byte 2:4 = Intel Manufacturer ID - 000157h, LS byte first.
o	Description
?	
-	EBh        ACL Update Completed
o	Response
?	Byte 1 - Completion Code
?	=00h - Success (Remaining standard Completion Codes are shown in Section 2.15).
?	=FFh - Unspecified Error
?	Byte 2:4 = Intel Manufacturer ID - 000157h, LS byte first.
o	Description
?	This command is sent by a MCTP PCIe bus owner to a Privileged Management Endpoint (PME) as a reply to the ACL Update Start command (see command above). This is to inform the PME that the process of updating all known MCTP ACL endpoints is completed and the PME can safely send security sensitive commands. The PME may decide to send the MCTP sensitive commands right on IPMI response to the Update ACL Start IPMI command, but it would be with the risk that not all endpoints are correctly updated yet, so some of the commands may not reach destination.

Net Function = S/E (04h) LUN = 00b
-	02h        Platform Event Message Intel ME Firmware Health Event
o	Byte 6 - Event Data 2 =0Eh - MCTP interface error. This is a notification that MCTP interface failure was detected and it is not functional any more. It may indicate the situation when MCTP was not configured by BIOS or a defect which may need a Host reset to recover from.
o	Byte 7 - Event Data 3
?	(For Event Data 2 (byte 6) equal to 0Eh)
-	=02h - No MCTP_SET_BUS_OWNER HECI message received by Intel ME on EOP arrival to ME, while MCTP stack is configured in Bus Owner Proxy mode
?	(For Event Data 2 (byte 6) equal to 10h)
-	=0Dh - MCTP bus owner
-	=0Eh - MCTP bus owner proxy

30h 3Eh (SDK General Application) - Net Function = SDK General Application (3Eh)
-	E8h        Get PCIe SMBus Slot Card Information
o	Byte 3 - Command Protocols Supported by the Proxy
?	[7:4] - Reserved
?	[3] - MCTP over SMBus
?	[2] - IPMI on PCIe SMBus (refer to the IPMI 2.0 spec.)
?	[1] - IPMB
o	[0] - UnknownByte 4 - Command Protocols Supported by this Card instance
?	[7:4] - Reserved
?	[3] - MCTP over SMBus
?	[2] - IPMI on PCIe SMBus
?	[1] - IPMB
?	[0] - Unknown

The plan as currently constituted makes the following assumptions: 

The wake-on-PECI PCS command has three values: 0, 1, and 2 as documented on the slide.  The value 3 is undefined. 
The mailbox operations are already validated and only need to be checked insofar as they have changed.

Configure wake-on-PECI to 0.  Enter package C6.   
Issue reads to the uncore CRs, core RdIAMSR,  core RdIAMSREx   
Ensure that they are not forward appropriate response by pcode.  - Error or system unavailable, cores in sleep etc.. 
Ensure that pcode returns error code for core msr MAILBOX_PECI_CC_THREAD_UNAVAILABLE. 

Configure wake-on-PECI to 1.  Enter package C6.   
Issue RdIAMSR and RdIAMSREx to cores 
Ensure they are not forwarded by pcode 
Ensure that pcode will return error code MAILBOX_PECI_CC_THREAD_UNAVAILABLE 
Issue reads to the uncore CRs and ensure that they are forwarded. Accessibility and correct read and write. 

Configure wake-on-PECI to 2.  Enter package C6.   
Issue reads to the uncore and ensure that they are forwarded.   
Issue RdIAMSR and RdIAMSREx to cores and ensure that they are forwarded.   
Issue RdIAMSR to disabled cores and ensure that they are not forwarded. 
Ensure that wake-on-PECI setting is persistent across patchload 
Ensure that wake-on-PECI setting is reset across warm reset 

Put some cores in C6 and others in other power states. 
Configure wake-on-PECI to 0 or 1.   
Issue RdIAMSR and RdIAMSREx to various cores and make sure reads always go through for cores not in C6. 
Stress test - BacktoBack transition from 0x2 to 0x1 and vice versa - reflects expected changes in behavior

Hi Foster,

  I'm having difficulty following your request for a test content update. I believe the current usage (as seen in the logs) of 0x2E 0xC8 (GetNmStatistics) to read "Mode 1 [Watts] on Domain 2 Memory subsystem" without per-component identifier "Policy field is ignored" is within the spec.

Please advise after reviewing 550710-nm-4-0-external-interface-spec


C8h Get Node Manager Statistics
Request
Byte 1:3 - Intel Manufacturer ID - 000157h, LS byte first
Byte 4 - 01h - Mode = Global power statistics in [Watts]
Byte 5 - 02h - Domain ID = Memory subsystem
Byte 5 [7] - Per-component control - allows for getting data for chosen domain component =0  Accumulated data for whole domain will be returned
Byte 6 - 00h - Policy ID / Component Identifier
For Modes 01h and 08h if bit 7 in Byte 5 is set to 1 then this field indicates component identifier for which data will be returned. Refer to Section 3.1.6 for description of this field.
For modes 11h-13h this field indicates the Policy ID for which the statistics are requested. 
For all other modes this field is ignored.

3.1.6 Component Identifier  
For Domain ID 02h (memory subsystem) component identifier is the CPU socket number (0-7) where 0 refers to lowest numbered address on the PECI bus associated with memory channels

## Option 2: Through Manufacturing mode (Available only in internal images) Root user, if not configured earlier, will be enabled automatically when entering the manufacturing mode. Applying AC Power along with pressing Power button for 15 seconds will force the system to enter the manufacturing mode. Password update will be enforced on first login attempt (without password). Note: This feature is controlled using validation_unsecure flags of EXTRA_IMAGE_FEATURES, and will not be available in commercial BMC image.

 cd /

 cd /miv-mivsoftware

~Update repository to the latest:
 git checkout master
 git pull

~Create a branch to make changes in the repository:
 git checkout -b <branch_name>

Modify files:
~Occasionally and before checking into origin - merge your branch with master
 git checkout master
 git pull
 git checkout <branch_name>
 git merge origin/master

~Checkin and push to origin:
 git status                        This will show changed files

~Verify changes applied to the file:
 git diff tests/testlib/riv_machine_config.py

 git add  tests/testlib/riv_machine_config.py                               - Add file to the commit

> PTU throttling to 1.0Ghz and TDP maxing out at ~55W (expect 165W)
From PM dump we can see that there are limits set that would match this throttling:
socket0.pcudata.pbm_resolved_cfg_pkg_pl2_msr.pbm_cfg_vector_pwr_lim=0x1bb - 55.375 W
socket0.pcudata.pbm_resolved_cfg_pkg_pl2_mmiopcs.pbm_cfg_vector_pwr_lim=0x1bb - 55.375 W
socket0.pcudata.pbm_resolved_cfg_pkg_pl1_msr.pbm_cfg_vector_pwr_lim=0x1ed - 61.625 W
socket0.pcudata.pbm_resolved_cfg_pkg_pl1_mmiopcs.pbm_cfg_vector_pwr_lim=0x1ed - 61.625 W

What we can also see there:
socket0.pcudata.pbm_pkg_max_power_setting=0x1ed
socket0.pcudata.pbm_pkg_min_power_setting=0x380
socket0.pcudata.resolved_tdp_power_of_sku=0x528
Which gives us TDP = 165 W, Min = 112 W, and Max = 61.625 W.

So, it looks like the CPU is fused incorrectly - max should probably not be less than Min. The limits that are set correspond to this Max value - PL1 set to 61.625 W and PL2 to 90% of that:
socket0.pcudata.pbm_pl2_discount.scalar=0xe6666666 - 0.899999999907
which resolves to 55.375 W (0x1ed = 493, floor(493 * 0.9) = 443, 443 / 8 = 55.375).

-58640
Steps:
Manual Method:
Navigate to miv-mivsoftware -> montana -> bin.  Next type the following:
montana.py -f miv_nm_power_limit_accuracy_d2.tdf
Automated method:
C:\miv-mivsoftware\batch>miv_nm_pwr_lim_acc_d2_batch.bat

Overview:
Testing the SPS FW ability to maintain a power limit being sweep across a range of values for the Memory (2) domain
Test Flow:
Must run Memory stress on SUT prior to starting test
Test will create a power policy on the Memory domain (D2) and then Sweep across either up or down from the max to min amount of allowable range of power.  Test will measure how accurately this is achieved.  Test will create a graph showing the programmed power limit and the actual limit (if passing the two lines will be drawn on top of one another).


-58668.3

Steps:
Run stress on the system under test.  Typically PTU on the memory.
Manually run test:
Navigate to miv-mivsoftware -> montana -> bin.  Next type the following:
montana.py -f miv_nm_power_limit_accuracy_d2.tdf
For Automation run:
c:\miv-mivsoftware\batch>miv_nm_pwr_lim_acc_d2_batch.bat

Overview:
Note: PTU will work on DDR4 and Crystal Ridge in 2LM.  For Crystal Ridge in 1LM you will need specific stress software that will work for 1LM, like MLC run in a Linux OS or AEP_PTU.
Testing the SPS FW ability to maintain a power policy accurately on the Memory (D2) domain
Test Flow
1. Start stress on the SUT (Target System)
2. Confirm BMC will communicate between Host and Target
3. Start power limit test which will do a PMCAPSWEEP.  In other words it will gradually increase then decrease(Sweep) a power management (PM) cap or limit across a range of allowed power limits on the system.  The test will run for the time specified in the time parameter inside the TDF under pmcapsweep.  The test will also create a makefile with a graphical image of the power limit the domain was set to against what the domain actually did.  If the test passes these two lines will be on top of one another and appear as one line.
4. After test is complete, results will be in CSV and makefile

-H 10.3.3.31 = host IP address
-U root = username
-P superuser = password
-t 2c = target address (Intel ME address)
-b 0x06 = bridge number (for Intel ME it is 6)
raw 0x2E = net function
0x46 = CPU IA MSR Read
Bytes 1:3 = Intel manufacture id
Byte 4 [7:3] = reserved
Byte 4 [2:0] = CPU number (socket 0)
Byte 5 = Thread ID
Byte 6 [7:0] = MSR address
Byte 7 [15:8] = MSR address
Byte 8 [7:3] = reserved
Byte 8 [2:0] = read length - number of bytes to read
= 1 - 1 byte
= 2 - 2 bytes (word)
= 3 - 4 bytes (double word)
= 4 - 8 bytes (quad word)

Byte 0:
Bit 0	No Error Flag.  Set, if there are no outstanding error conditions on this device/slot.  If Bit 0 is set to "1", all other bits in this register must be "0".
 
Bit 1	Device Faulty Flag.  Set, if this device has exhibited some hardware or data fault.  The GEM424 displays the device fault state externally on each slot LED.  Optionally, the GEM424 can be configured to toggle the pin configured to (function type Global Alarm) when this bit is set for any valid slot.  

Bit 3	In Failed Array Flag.  Set, if this device is in an array with an error on any member device.
Bit 4	In Critical Array Flag.  Set, if this device is in an array that was previously fault-tolerant and has become non-fault-tolerant. 

Bit 7	Unconfigured Drive Flag.  This bit will be set for all device slots that do not contain a drive that is included in an array configuration. This excludes slots containing a drive that is currently part of an array, configured as a hot spare, or that failed while part of an array.

[Worked]
Having two systems enabled sanity checks on sightings and unblocked test execution.
The XCC (BMC) features proved immensely helpful including remote access, remote system event log, FW update, & service data.
Serial debug port gave confidence that the system was not hung during long (30+min) boot cycles, gave visibility to hangs and exceptions.
Automating Power cycling resulted in useful data analysis (boot time variations, total memory variations) and saved manual execution time.
Benchmarks including iLVSS & Memtest proved stressful enough to find bugs.


[Worked internally]
Pre-sync meetings promoted 'one voice' presentation and improved quality.
Glasgow allowed multiple people to seamlessly cooperate with and improve test execution. (Special thanks to Stephen VL, Scott M, Dave R)
Specific space and power requirements were met by our lab.
Adding host NUC's to the SUTs enabled smooth debugging and execution.


[Needs improvement]
Long boot times impacted setup an execution early in the program.
Need a clear path from sighting to fix, trim out layers of communication where possible.
A TOPS document would be helpful: BKC update BKM, boot time expectations, how to swap compute boards, etc.
The charter for this validation effort was unclear.  This lead to baseline gathering rather than a focus on enabling developers.  Time would be better spend with a development enabling focus and slowly expand coverage naturally (i.e. boot times, stability, recovery).


[Internal improvement]
Holding on to old BKC versions gave diminishing returns on investment, old bugs needed to be re-verified with latest code.
Spent a lot of time moving DIMMs around to get things right, having spares available (AEP, DDR4) would have helped.
Bugs and sightings filed in our HSDES are not visible to PAE. Add hoc syncs helped, but visibility could improve if PAE held a stake in our meetings.

wireshark-dev@wireshark.org

	This patch allows the IPMI dissector to read IPMI 2.0 (RMCP Plus) packets per the spec at

	http://www.intel.com/design/servers/ipmi/spec.htm

	Specifically Table 13-8, RMCP/RMCP+ Packet Format for IPMI via Ethernet

	Its not quite complete, [OEM IANA] and [OEM Payload ID] are missing.  These are not present by default (i.e. IPMI Messages) and potentially go beyond the scope of this dissector.  The auth_offset changes should allow them to easily be added at a later time If needed.  Ive occasionally been getting [Malformed packet] at the end of the (much more descriptive) RMCPP packet descriptions, probably due to slight padding differences not dealt with yet.

	The patch was designed not to break IPMI 1.5, and it works from what Ive tested.

	The patch was mostly replacing "authtype ? :" with "auth_offset +" where appropriate.  Im not a big fan of the ternary operator, and it didnt help when a third option came in (authtype=6 is RMCPP).  "auth_offset" may be redundant with "offset" already in  use.  I didnt want to risk changing the flow too much so the two are separate.

	(Diff created against /trunk/epan/dissectors/packet-ipmi.c Revision 18412)

25244 - apiKey (Updated)


Failures are test/setup issues and not firmware failures.  Once the key is locked, by design, it cannot be unlocked.  

IPMI 2.0 13.34.1	Random Number Key "the BMC includes an option for the key to be locked so that run-time software cannot change the key."

Clearing nvram did not unlock the key since that area is protected.  Running this test requires help from a developer to _really_ clear the nvram, leaving the key in an unlocked state.

Test needs to be updated:

1) The test setup shold test if the key is locked and give instructions to clear nvram to unlock key (with developers help).
2) A logical prgression of steps in the test would be get, set, get, lock, (expect 0x80 from subsequent get/sets).

Related tracker#25498  "BIOS ignores SOL configuration parameters" would bypass the need for Setup. 




25498 BIOS ignores SOL configuration parameters

Console redirection requires BIOS setup.

Currently a remote console connection requires local configuration in the BIOS
Specifically, changing the 'virtual com' buad rate to 19200 and disabling com2 before console redirection will work properly.
(see tracker# for details on setup)
Setup is complex and not intuative to the user, it also defeats the purpouse of a remote administration.

Recommendation to fix:


BIOS can use the standard IPMI 2.0 'Get SOL Configuration Parameters Command' (Section 26.3) to retrieve the proper settings.  The 'SOL Activating Command' may be useful as well.

(using DOS cmdtool for clarity)
Get SOL Configuration Parameter 5 non-volatile bit rate:
   cmdtool 20 30 22 01 05 00 00 
   20 34 22 00 11 07
Get SOL Configuration Parameter 6 volatile bit rate (optional):
   cmdtool 20 30 22 01 06 00 00 
   20 34 22 00 11 07

7h: 19.2 kbps (Support for bit rates other than 19.2 kbps is optional)
8h: 38.4 kbps
9h: 57.6 kbps
Ah: 115.2 kbps

#-----------------------------------------------------------------------
#	Function:	_ftf_test_stop
#	Purpose:	Stop a test.
#	Scope:		Private.
#-----------------------------------------------------------------------
proc _ftf_test_stop { } {
	return [_ftf_ui_event STOPREQ]
}

#-----------------------------------------------------------------------
#	Function:	_ftf_test_pause
#	Purpose:	Pause a test.
#	Scope:		Private.
#-----------------------------------------------------------------------
proc _ftf_test_pause { } {
	global _FTF_Running
	global _FTF_UI_Event
	set _FTF_UI_Event(PAUSEREQ) 1
		
	.f0.pause_button configure -text "Resume" -command _ftf_test_resume -state active
	
	
	#pause
	set time0 [clock seconds]
	set count 0
	array set eventArray [ftf_eventcheck]
	while {$eventArray(PAUSEREQ) && !$eventArray(STOPREQ)} {
			while {[expr $count + $time0] == [clock seconds]} {
				array set eventArray [ftf_eventcheck]
			}
			incr count
			
			ftf_status "Paused for $seconds count ('Resume' to continue)"
			
	}
	ftf_status ""
	
	#if {$eventArray(STOPREQ)} { set _FTF_Running ? }
	#stop returned?
	return $_FTF_Running
}

#-----------------------------------------------------------------------
#	Function:	_ftf_test_resume
#	Purpose:	Resume a test.
#	Scope:		Private.
#-----------------------------------------------------------------------
proc _ftf_test_resume { } {
	global _FTF_Running
	
	global _FTF_UI_Event
	set _FTF_UI_Event(PAUSEREQ) 0
	
	.f0.pause_button configure -text "Pause" -command _ftf_test_pause -state active
}
